newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM raps reporter for meeting Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM raps reporter for meeting Peru rebels.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday criticised a Japanese journalist for entering the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, saying his actions could have harmed efforts to resolve the hostage crisis.
"It is very regrettable," a Foreign Ministry official quoted Hashimoto as telling reporters travelling with him on an eight-day tour of Southeast Asian nations.
"An act like that could create unforeseeable circumstances and disrupt the Peruvian government's efforts for a peaceful resolution and the release of all hostages," he said.

A Japanese reporter for a subsidiary of Japanese television station TV Asahi and his interpreter entered the residence on Tuesday at the invitation of the rebels of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
They left about two hours later, only to be arrested and driven away by anti-terrorism police to their headquarters in downtown Lima, where their notebooks and camera were confiscated.
TV Asahi named the two as Peruvian interpreter Victor Borja and New York-based reporter Tsuyoshi Hitomi.

Their entry into the residence, as well as that on New Year's Eve by a bigger group of journalists, was condemned by Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi as "damaging to the seriousness and fluidity of talks".
A spokesman for TV Asahi said the company did not instruct the reporter to enter the residence and his supervisor in Lima was not aware of Hitomi's attempts, Kyodo news agency reported.

The Marxist rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17 and took about 500 hostages including ambassadors and senior Peruvian government officials. Most of them were later released, leaving 74 hostages remaining.
